transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-18
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez (Redwood); Oliver Grant, Priya Singh, Noah Wallace (Archipelago Payments)
---
Summary: quick product walkthrough focused on data handling and retention controls in Redwood (console + API + Optimize). Customer is evaluating for payments telemetry and wants strong PII redaction, per-route retention toggles, and enterprise audit logs for compliance.
Topics: logging redaction, request storage toggles, PII detection, KMS integration, retention windows, dedicated/private options, benchmarking next steps.

00:00 Oliver: Okay we can kick off, thanks for doing this. we're on a pretty tight timeline, CFO wants a vendor decision by end of month.
00:12 Maya: Yeah totally, we'll keep it focused  quick overview of retention controls and then a live demo in the console of toggles and redaction. Diego will show the runtime bits.
00:20 Priya: hi, quick intro: I'm Priya, security. main items: SOC2, SSO/SAML, encrypted at rest incl KMS, and ability to not persist PII or to redact before storage.
00:35 Diego: great, we have those  the console has per-route storage toggles plus configurable redaction rules. note though, there's a couple of deployment modes: hosted vs dedicated vs private  retention and audit options differ slightly.
00:50 Noah: when you say per-route, is that per API key or per model endpoint?
00:59 Diego: good question  it's per route in the Redwood config which maps to model+path+key. you can set storage: never-store, store-transient, store-persist. also you can set automatic PII detectors to redact names, emails, acct numbers before anything hits persistent logs.
01:20 Oliver: can we see that in the console?
01:26 Maya: yeah let's share screen  opening Redwood Console -> Settings -> Data Retention.
01:35 [screen share start]
01:40 Diego: top-level policy, you can set org default retention window, encryption settings and KMS key ARN for customer-managed keys. below that are route-level overrides. here I'm toggling a route for /payments/validate to never-store.
01:57 Priya: hmm, does never-store still keep ephemeral traces for debugging? like request IDs for observability?
02:06 Diego: by default never-store will keep a short-lived request ID in ephemeral logs for 1 hour for debugging  not persisted to long term. there's an option to scrub even those traces. sometimes teams keep a 24-48 hour ephemeral buffer to root cause incidents.
02:22 Priya: we need the option to disable even ephemeral traces for certain routes that touch PHI.
02:29 Diego: yes, we can toggle ephemeral retention down to zero on a per-route basis. note that will reduce our ability to debug post-mortem, which you guys already know; tradeoff.
02:40 Noah: and redaction  is it client-side or server-side? we'd prefer server-side real-time redaction so nothing lands in logs.
02:49 Diego: Redwood supports server-side redaction. two layers: simple pattern-based redaction (regexes you provide) and ML-based PII detectors that run inline. ML detector masks tokens before storage. we can also run a deterministic tokenization + hash for certain fields for analytics without storing raw values.
03:12 Priya: what about PCI card numbers? we can't store PANs full length.
03:17 Maya: for PCI we recommend tokenization plus redaction, plus a dedicated flow that never persists raw PANs. Redwood has built-in Luhn-based detector and a rule block that will either mask the middle digits or drop the field depending on your policy.
03:33 Oliver: encryption  KMS integration, audit logs  is everything audit-trailable for compliance?
03:40 Diego: yes, audit logs are stored separately and you can configure retention and export to your SIEM. audit logs include who changed retention settings and config rollouts. decryption operations with customer-managed keys are logged.
03:52 Priya: are audit logs tamper-evident or append-only?
03:56 Diego: currently append-only with signed entries; we also provide optional export to your S3 bucket or push to Splunk/Datadog. for highest assurance we recommend pushing out to your own storage and enabling your retention/immutability policies.
04:12 Noah: what's the model in hosted mode  do you get any request storage by default?
04:17 Maya: hosted mode stores request/response for 30 days by default for debugging and model quality, but you can opt out per route or at org-level under the data retention settings. Dedicated and Private give you more control and typically default to shorter retention.
04:31 Oliver: ok cost question  storing every request costs. how do we estimate unit costs?
04:36 Maya: Redwood Console Optimize module provides token-level cost breakdown and can simulate cost impact of retention settings. if you disable storage entirely you'll remove those storage costs but might increase support overhead. we can run a delta cost estimate if you share sample traffic.
04:52 Priya: can we set retention based on data classification? e.g., if field classified PHI -> auto-never-store?
04:58 Diego: yes, we have a tagging/classification pipeline: you can attach metadata to requests (headers or attributes), and policy engine will apply retention actions. you can also run content inspection and classify on the fly.
05:12 [30s pause as Diego toggles policy]
05:40 Diego: showing a rule: if header X-Sensitive: true then route action = never-store; else apply default. policy changes are versioned and you can roll back.
05:52 Priya: is there an audit for policy changes?
05:55 Diego: yes change author, timestamp, diff of rule is in audit logs.
06:02 Oliver: about deletion  if we decide to purge historical stored requests, is there a way to do bulk delete and certify deletion to auditors?
06:10 Maya: we provide bulk delete APIs and a deletion job that produces a deletion report you can hand to auditors. for customer-managed storage we can also run a one-time scrub.
06:21 Priya: retention windows  do you support tiered retention? dev logs 7 days, prod logs 90 days?
06:28 Diego: yep, route-level retention can be set to any window and we support retention classes: ephemeral, short, medium, long. you can map environments or tags to classes.
06:38 Noah: does the ML PII detector ever false-positive and cause data loss for debugging?
06:44 Diego: there are tradeoffs  ML detector can be tuned with allow-lists and confidence thresholds. we usually recommend a two-step: mask for storage but also keep hashed tokens for analytics so you don't lose signposting for debugging.
06:58 Priya: what about redaction rules for legal holds? sometimes legal requires retention of certain records despite PII.
07:05 Maya: we support legal holds: a retention override that prevents deletion for specified request IDs or time windows. it's an admin-only action and captured in audit logs.
07:16 Oliver: ok can you show an API flow  what does a request look like if we send X-Archipelago-PII: true?
07:24 Diego: sure  switching to API examples in the doc pane. here's a sample POST to /validate with header X-Retention: never-store. the runtime reads the header and applies policy before writing to storage.
07:40 Priya: is that header authenticated? could an attacker set it to hide traces?
07:45 Diego: good catch  header-based decisions should be validated and whitelisted per API key; Redwood supports header provenance checks and policy to ignore client-supplied retention headers unless signed by your gateway.
07:58 Noah: performance implications  does inline ML PII detection add latency?
08:05 Diego: small overhead, typically 10-60ms depending on model and sequence length. for high-performance routes you can run a lightweight regex-based filter or offload redaction to a dedicated redaction worker in the pipeline.
08:20 Oliver: would dedicated mode reduce that overhead?
08:23 Diego: dedicated gives you control over instance sizing and colocated redaction workers, so yes you can tune for lower latency. also dedicated/private allows you to run quantized models locally which reduces CPU.
08:36 Priya: for our SOC2 doc review we need sample retention policy screenshots and the retention export format  CSV or JSON?
08:44 Maya: export can be JSON or CSV and we can include metadata for each deleted/preserved item. I'll send sample exports.
08:51 [small crosstalk]
09:00 Diego: one more note  the KV cache and prefix cache used for throughput is separate from persistent storage. we scrub caches on policy change and do not persist cache content beyond configured windows.
09:13 Priya: I saw a doc earlier that said "KV cache" but someone wrote K V cash in the doc  minor but watch naming in docs.
09:20 Diego: haha noted.
09:24 Oliver: able to role-based restrict who can change retention?
09:27 Diego: yes RBAC  admin roles, security role, auditor role (read-only). you can restrict route-level policy edits to a handful of users and track via audit logs.
09:36 Priya: SSO and SCIM?
09:38 Maya: SAML SSO plus SCIM for provisioning; we support enforced 2FA for admin roles.
09:44 Noah: what about e-discovery for legal? we need bulk export and chain of custody.
09:49 Diego: export with signed manifests and optional timestamped notarization; we support push to your archival storage and provide a manifest for chain of custody.
10:02 Oliver: any gotchas with using customer-managed KMS?
10:06 Diego: you control the key lifecycle; backup and rotation are your responsibility  Redwood stores encrypted blobs and we do not hold plaintext without your key. note that key rotation can require re-encrypting stored artifacts if you rotate outside of recommended flow.
10:22 Priya: demonstration of redaction rules  can you create a custom regex and test live?
10:28 Diego: yes creating one now  regex for credit card pattern, run a sample.
10:40 [typing]
11:00 Diego: sample payload: {"card_number":"4111 1111 1111 1111","name":"JANE DOE"} -> shows in pipeline as MASKED: 4111 **** **** 1111 and name -> [REDACTED]. this is what gets stored when store-transient is selected.
11:20 Priya: will the stored record still include a hash of the full PAN so we can detect duplicates?
11:26 Diego: yes we can store a salted hash field if you opt-in; hashing is deterministic per-salt so you can dedupe without storing PAN.
11:34 Oliver: audit  show a quick policy change timeline.
11:39 Diego: clicking into policy history  here you can see author, diff, and ability to revert.
11:46 Priya: curious about long-term model quality data  if we opt out of storing requests, will model performance monitoring suffer?
11:53 Maya: Redwood Optimize can work with synthetic or sampled data; we also support hashed metadata to get QPS and token breakdowns without raw content. many customers allow limited sample storage for evals.
12:10 Noah: want to raise a blocker: our compliance team won't accept vendor that stores any PANs even encrypted unless in our own vault. so private/on-prem might be necessary.
12:20 Maya: understood  private deployment is an option, we can ship private control plane and your infra can manage keys and storage. that said there are integration overheads and longer provisioning.
12:31 Oliver: can you scope that in terms of timeline/cost?
12:34 Maya: typical private deployment onboarding is 6-10 weeks and additional licensing; we can provide a rough SOW. I'll follow up.
12:42 Priya: about log forwarding  can Redwood push all audit logs to our Splunk with guaranteed delivery?
12:47 Diego: yes we have log-forwarding with retry and acknowledgement patterns; for high-assurance we recommend also exporting to S3 as a secondary sink.
12:58 [brief pause]
13:12 Diego: switching to the API example for toggles  here's an admin POST to /org/policies with JSON body that sets retention windows per route.
13:28 Oliver: do we get a dry-run mode to simulate effect of rules on historical data?
13:33 Diego: yes we have a policy simulator; you can run it against a sample of historical logs to see which records would be redacted or deleted.
13:44 Priya: perfect  we'll need that for legal to show impact.
13:49 Maya: next, want to demo the deletion job and report.
13:56 [screen share: deletion job UI]
14:05 Diego: launching a deletion job for requests older than 90 days in dev stencil  job runs and produces a report with counts, sample IDs, and checksums for auditor verification.
14:21 Priya: checksum algorithm? sha256?
14:24 Diego: yes sha256, salted.
14:28 Oliver: about request-scoped toggles  say we have a partner gateway that needs longer logs, can we grant partner access to a subset of logs?
14:36 Diego: you can configure cross-account access via IAM policies and export to partner bucket; Redwood handles access controls and masking on export.
14:47 Noah: two quick product questions  can we automate retention changes via Terraform? and is there a swagger spec?
14:55 Maya: yes we have an infra-as-code provider and full OpenAPI spec.
15:02 Priya: for the SOC2 q's  can you show us the section in the doc where you describe key rotation and access?
15:08 Maya: opening SOC2 section  shows KMS integration, rotation best practices, and role separation. I'll email the excerpt.
15:16 [20s silence as Maya composes email]
15:40 Oliver: ok let's talk about next steps and pilot  we'd like a trial that enforces never-store on card routes and lets us run 100k validations per day for two weeks.
15:51 Maya: we can provision a dedicated trial for that. Diego will run benchmarking and we'll provide cost estimates.
15:58 Priya: and we'll run our compliance questionnaire in parallel  expect follow-ups.
16:04 Diego: quick note on logs: if you route logs to your S3 we can rotate per lifecycle policy and keep backups for your archival.
16:12 Oliver: client-side  do you have SDKs that integrate redaction before sending?
16:17 Maya: yes SDKs in Node/Python with pre-send scrubbing helpers, but most clients prefer server-side for central control.
16:28 Priya: regarding legal hold again: we need chain-of-custody AND ability to lock retention policies so they cannot be rolled back without multi-person approval.
16:37 Diego: we have approval workflows (2-person approve) for legal hold toggles and policy lock.
16:45 Noah: any known limitations or bugs in the current retention UI?
16:49 Diego: minor one  under heavy load the policy simulator can slow; we recommend sampling runs for large corpora. fix in next patch. transcript note: simulator may be called "policy sim" in some docs.
17:05 Priya: can we see a sample export manifest now?
17:10 Diego: sending a sample manifest to chat  contains file list, sha256, timestamps.
17:18 Oliver: will you share the recording and screenshots?
17:21 Maya: yes will send.
17:26 [end of screen share]
17:30 Priya: security question  we need proof that when never-store is enabled there is no hot path to accidentally write to persistent logs.
17:38 Diego: we've got tests and a verification suite that runs nightly; we can share a compliance test report and an architecture diagram that shows the redaction pipeline prior to the log writer.
17:50 Oliver: great. cost implication again: if we hash tokens for analytics  any performance/regulatory tradeoffs?
17:59 Diego: hashing adds CPU but is low overhead; regulatory depends on whether hashed values are considered identifiers in your jurisdiction. consult legal.
18:12 Priya: any client references with payments and redaction enabled?
18:17 Maya: we have a few financials  I'll share anonymized case studies (Cedarbanks, MeridianPay references).
18:27 Noah: ok let's recap next steps.
18:31 Maya: recap: 1) We'll send SOC2 and retention docs + sample export 2) Dieg o will run dedicated benchmarking and share results 3) Provision trial dedicated instance with never-store on card routes 4) Customer to return compliance questionnaire and sample redaction policy.
18:49 Priya: small correction  Diego spelled as Diego.
18:52 Maya: fixed in notes.
18:55 Oliver: timeline?
18:57 Maya: SOC2 + docs by 2026-08-20, trial provision estimate and SOW by 2026-08-21, benchmarks by 2026-08-25.
19:10 Noah: thanks, that's good. we'll schedule follow-up after we review.
19:15 [meeting end]
